about: The direct step's live run of the design example '01-laser-mirror' (20 Oct 2026): Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) through the gateway, measured by the engine's executor (web/export/shots.js checkPlan). Each round: the plan the model answered, and what the executor's checks said of it.

lesson.question: What happens to the light when it hits the mirror?
lesson.answer: It bounces off. The angle going out is the same as the angle coming in.

payload.concept: light reflects off a mirror: the angle in equals the angle out

plan.title: Angle in equals angle out
plan.about: Light from a laser goes straight to a mirror and bounces off it at the same angle it came in.

source.question: What happens to the light when it hits the mirror?
source.answer: It bounces off. The angle going out is the same as the angle coming in.

story.says: Light comes out of the laser.
It goes in a straight line to the mirror.
It goes straight on to the target.
The whole path: laser, mirror, target.
The angle going in is the same as the angle going out.

shots.intent: Start on the cause: the laser and the thin line of light leaving its tip, placed left so the light has room to go right, where the story goes.

audit.question: Can a child see a thin bright line of light coming out of the laser?

shots.intent: Ride along the beam at a walking pace over a held moment: the straight line is the path the light takes, and the camera takes it too.

audit.question: Does the camera move along one straight line of light from the laser to the mirror?

shots.intent: Stop where the light turns: the bright spot on the mirror, with the light coming in and going out of it.

audit.question: Can a child see the light hit the mirror and leave it going a new way?

shots.intent: Ride the bounced light on to the target at the same pace and scale: after the bounce it is still a straight line, and it ends on the target.

audit.question: Does the camera follow the bounced light in a straight line up to the target?

shots.intent: Back up from the target until the whole path of the light fills the picture, square on: laser, mirror, target, and the V the light makes.

audit.question: When the camera stops, is the whole path of the light, from the laser to the mirror to the target, in the picture?

shots.intent: Ease in on the corner of the V, square on, until the two rays and the mirror fill the picture; then the dashed normal and two arcs with their measured angles appear, and hold for the question.

audit.question: Can a Grade 4 child see that the angle going in and the angle going out are the same?

plan.notes: The run is still (the laser is on from the start and nothing moves), so the whole video films one held moment at release and the camera tells the story: follow the light, stop on the bounce, follow it on, back up to the whole V, then push in on the equal angles. The last two shots are square on (yaw 0, pitch 1) because an angle in the machine plane reads true only when the plane faces the camera. Every window stays under 2.05 m so the beam's core stays visible. The travels ride over a frozen moment: light is instant, and the ride is only a way of looking.
